NVIDIA disclosed in its latest quarterly earnings report that price hikes for memory and other key components had exceeded expectations. Therefore, its gross margin is also projected to shrink from 75% to 71-72% by 4Q26.

Consequently, finding alternative solutions to alleviate supply shortages and cost pressures has become an urgent priority for OEMs and ODMs. In this context, Chinese component suppliers, which historically struggled to penetrate the supply chains of international electronics brands, have unexpectedly emerged as a viable new solution.

major PC brands such as Dell, HP, ASUS, and Acer have completed
DRAM qualifications for Chinese memory supplier CXMT this year. Furthermore, these brands have already begun incorporating CXMT components in small volumes for select entry-level consumer PC/NB models
targeted at non-US markets. The scope of qualifications for components from alternative sources is steadily extending from memory to other active and passive components. TrendForce’s investigations indicate that, facilitated by Chinese ODMs such as Huaqin, LCFC, and Luxshare, brands like HP, ASUS, and Acer have initiated qualification processes for MLCC products from Viiyong and CCTC.
